headline.headline: WHEELER BLANKS MARLINS AS PHILLIES ROLL 7-0
headline.deck: Zack Wheeler dominates in a two-hour, 45-minute gem before 39,241 at Citizens Bank Park
headline.body:
PHILADELPHIA — Zack Wheeler was untouchable Monday night, shutting out the Miami Marlins across nine innings as the Philadelphia Phillies rolled to a 7-0 victory before a crowd of 39,241 at Citizens Bank Park. Wheeler, the ace of Philadelphia's rotation, never let Miami threaten, holding the Marlins scoreless in every inning while his offense provided a steady drumbeat of support across the game's nine frames.

The Phillies broke open the scoring with a run in the second inning, added two more in the third, and piled on with a pair in the fifth before finishing with two additional runs in the eighth. Trea Turner was hit by a pitch from Miami's Kempner during the contest, but the play of the night belonged to Wheeler, who needed just two hours and 45 minutes to complete his masterwork. Miami was unable to dent the Philadelphia run prevention at any point in the evening.

The shutout loss continued a difficult stretch for the Marlins, who were held without a run from the first pitch to the last. For the Phillies, the commanding victory underscored the value of a healthy Wheeler at the top of their rotation, and the Citizens Bank Park faithful went home satisfied after a dominant performance from start to finish.

secondary.headline: NATIONALS SURGE PAST ROYALS 7-3 ON CREWS HOMER, FIVE-RUN FIFTH
secondary.deck: Dylan Crews blasts his fourth home run as Washington extends its home winning streak to four games
secondary.body:
WASHINGTON — Dylan Crews launched his fourth home run of the season and the Nationals erupted for five runs in the fifth inning to bury the Kansas City Royals 7-3 Monday afternoon at Nationals Park. The five-run fifth broke a game that had been knotted early, and Washington never looked back, extending its home winning streak to four games before an announced crowd of 14,444.

Kansas City scratched across a run in the fourth inning and added two more in the fifth before Washington's big frame put the game away for good. The Royals left 12 runners on base, a number that told the story of a team that generated chances but could not convert them. Doubles from Caglianone, Loftin and Wood filled in the box score for a Kansas City squad now sitting at 29-44, fifth in the AL Central, while the Nationals improved to 38-35 with a game that lasted just two hours and 30 minutes.

secondary.headline: DOLAN'S PREGAME SPEECH TO KNICKS SURFACES BEFORE PIVOTAL PLAYOFF RUN
secondary.deck: Knicks owner James Dolan urged players to sacrifice personally for a championship in an April address
secondary.body:
NEW YORK — Before the Knicks ever tipped off in the 2026 playoffs, owner James Dolan stood in front of his players and asked them to give up something of themselves in pursuit of an NBA championship. Details of that April speech, delivered ahead of the postseason, surfaced Monday as New York navigates the second round of the playoffs with a title-or-bust pressure that Dolan himself helped manufacture.

The message from Dolan was described as impassioned, a rare direct address from an owner who has long been one of the most polarizing figures in professional basketball. Whether the speech serves as motivation or distraction remains an open question as the Knicks push deeper into May. What is clear is that Dolan, who has waited decades for a championship return to Madison Square Garden, is leaving nothing unsaid as this postseason unfolds.

secondary.headline: GIOLITO SHUTS OUT PADRES AS CARDINALS WIN 3-0 IN SWIFT 2:08 CONTEST
secondary.deck: Lucas Giolito picks up the win as St. Louis holds San Diego without a run and strands just three baserunners
secondary.body:
ST. LOUIS — Lucas Giolito earned the victory Monday as the St. Louis Cardinals shut out the San Diego Padres 3-0 in one of the more efficient games of the early summer, a contest completed in just two hours and eight minutes before 26,973 at Busch Stadium. The Cardinals did their damage in the fourth inning with two runs and added a third in the fifth, then locked down San Diego for the remainder of the afternoon.

The Padres finished with just three runners left on base, a remarkably low total that reflected how thoroughly St. Louis controlled the pitching side of the ledger. Doubles from Burleson and Crooks provided the offensive highlights for the Cardinals, who stranded 14 of their own baserunners but got just enough production when it mattered. The Padres, held without an extra-base hit, have now been shut out as the Cardinals' rotation continues to show its depth.

column.headline: WHEELER'S BRILLIANCE IS A REMINDER OF WHAT AN ACE ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE
column.body:
There is a version of the Phillies that plays small ball, scrapes runs together and hopes the bullpen holds. Monday night at Citizens Bank Park was not that version. When Zack Wheeler is locked in, Philadelphia does not need to manufacture anything. The runs come, the outs come even faster, and 39,241 people get to watch a professional dismantle an opponent with the kind of quiet authority that only the very best pitchers can project. A shutout in two hours and 45 minutes is not luck. That is command.

The Marlins were never a factor. Not in the second inning, not in the fifth, not at any moment when Miami might have crept back into a game Wheeler had decided was already over. The Phillies have real aspirations this summer, and Wheeler is the reason those aspirations are grounded in something more than hope. When he pitches, the math changes. Every contender in the National League should be paying attention.

story.headline: REDS BURY METS WITH NINE-RUN FIRST TWO INNINGS IN 12-0 ROUT
story.deck: Bleday and Suárez homer as Cincinnati turns out Gotham's lights early
story.body:
CINCINNATI, June 15 — The New York Mets never had a chance. The Cincinnati Reds erupted for three runs in the first inning and piled on six more in the second, building a 9-0 lead before the Mets could blink, and coasted to a 12-0 shellacking before 19,853 fans at Great American Ball Park on Monday night.

Joey Bleday launched his 13th home run of the season and Eugenio Suárez added his seventh as the Reds kept the Mets scoreless through all nine innings. New York's pitching staff hit Matt McLain with a pitch, surrendered three more runs in the eighth, and watched its team strand a staggering 28 runners on base — a testament to an offense that loaded the bases repeatedly but could not deliver against Cincinnati's arms. Nick Pintaro drew the hit-by-pitch call against McLain. Bo Bichette and Elly De La Cruz each contributed doubles, while Jake Dunn and Curtis Stewart added stolen bases to keep the Reds moving all night.

The Mets' futility stood in sharp contrast to what was happening across the sport Monday. In Philadelphia, Zack Wheeler earned the win as the Phillies blanked Miami 7-0, with J.T. Realmuto hitting his fifth homer. In Detroit, Spencer Torkelson slugged his 12th home run and the Tigers pounded the Astros 9-3, while Byron Buxton's 23rd blast led the Twins past Texas 4-2. Lucas Giolito pitched St. Louis to a 3-0 shutout of San Diego, and Pete Crow-Armstrong hit a home run, double and triple to power the Cubs past Colorado 5-4 in the ninth.

story.headline: PETERSON WORKS OUT FOR WIZARDS ONLY AS SPLITTER TAKES BULLS JOB AND DOLAN SPEECH SURFACES
story.deck: Top prospect Darryn Peterson signals Washington preference as Chicago makes surprising coaching hire.
story.body:
Highly touted prospect Darryn Peterson is working out exclusively with the Washington Wizards ahead of the 2026 NBA Draft, according to ESPN's Shams Charania, a strong signal that Peterson has communicated his preference to land in the nation's capital. The move gives Washington significant leverage and excitement around a rebuilding franchise desperately searching for a cornerstone piece to build around for the next decade.

Meanwhile, the Chicago Bulls are finalizing a deal with former San Antonio Spurs center Tiago Splitter to become the franchise's new head coach, Charania also reported Tuesday. Splitter, who won two NBA championships alongside Tim Duncan and Tony Parker in San Antonio, has spent recent years transitioning into coaching and front-office work in Brazil and Europe, earning a reputation as a tactically sharp basketball mind with deep ties to the Gregg Popovich coaching tree.

Elsewhere around the league, former champion Kendrick Perkins publicly called on the San Antonio Spurs to move on from De'Aaron Fox, arguing the veteran point guard has not proven he can lead a young contender in the right direction. The comments arrive amid swirling speculation about Fox's long-term fit alongside rising Spurs star Victor Wembanyama. Additionally, a James Dolan speech from April surfaced in which the embattled Knicks owner urged his players to sacrifice personal glory for a championship, a rare and emotional moment that New York players described as genuinely moving before their playoff run.

story.headline: NHL OPENS PROBE INTO BABCOCK'S ABRUPT RESIGNATION FROM COLUMBUS BLUE JACKETS
story.deck: League scrutinizes circumstances surrounding coach's sudden departure last September
story.body:
The NHL has launched a formal investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mike Babcock's resignation as head coach of the Columbus Blue Jackets last September, the league confirmed Tuesday. The inquiry signals that officials believe there may be more to Babcock's sudden exit than a simple parting of ways, and it raises the specter of a deeper institutional reckoning for a franchise that has struggled both on the ice and behind the scenes in recent years.

Babcock, 63, resigned from the Columbus post without public explanation after less than two full seasons behind the Blue Jackets bench. The veteran bench boss, who previously coached the Detroit Red Wings and Toronto Maple Leafs before a controversy-clouded tenure in Toronto ended in his firing in 2019, had returned to the NHL with Columbus in what was widely seen as a professional rehabilitation. The investigation's scope and timeline have not been disclosed, but sources familiar with the situation say league officials have already begun reaching out to Blue Jackets personnel.

Meanwhile, the hockey world absorbed additional news Tuesday as oddsmakers installed the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes as the early favorites to repeat in 2027 at +700, with the Colorado Avalanche close behind at +800 and the Vegas Golden Knights rounding out the top tier. In the women's game, the PWHL's incoming Las Vegas expansion franchise named Kim Weiss as its inaugural head coach, with Weiss arriving after two seasons in an assistant role at the collegiate level.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL ROSTERS TAKE SHAPE THIS SPRING
story.deck: Several veteran signal-callers find new homes as teams retool for 2026 campaign.
story.body:
The NFL offseason reshuffling continued in earnest this week, with front offices across the league making aggressive moves at quarterback after a winter of roster evaluations following Super Bowl LX. The Pittsburgh Steelers, still searching for a long-term answer under center after years of instability, emerged as the most aggressive suitors in a thin free-agent market, while the New Orleans Saints and Cleveland Browns also pursued upgrades at the position with varying degrees of urgency and cap flexibility.

The 2026 NFL Draft, held last month in Washington D.C., produced its share of first-round surprises, and several rookie quarterbacks selected in April are already drawing attention at organized team activity sessions beginning this week. Scouts who attended Colorado's pro day in March had raved about the arm talent of the top prospects, and early OTA reports suggest at least two of the top-10 picks are pushing for immediate starting roles rather than the traditional redshirt seasons their teams had originally envisioned for them.

On the trade front, the Las Vegas Raiders completed a blockbuster deal shipping a package of picks to the Tennessee Titans in exchange for a proven veteran presence on the offensive line, addressing what coaches identified as the team's most glaring weakness from the 2025 season. Raiders general manager Tom Telesco called the move a cornerstone of a broader rebuild aimed at returning Las Vegas to playoff contention by the fall.
